name: 90/90 Hamstring Stretch
overview: The 90/90 hamstring stretch is a flexibility exercise that targets the hamstrings and glutes. It involves lying on your back with one leg in front, bent at 90 degrees, and hinging forward at the hips. This stretch is essential for improving hip mobility, reducing lower back stiffness, and preventing muscle imbalances between legs.
benefits: Improves hip mobility and range of motion
Reduces lower back stiffness and discomfort
Enhances athletic performance and running economy

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-3 (3 seconds hold, 1 second release, 3 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight only, can apply gentle resistance if needed
trainingParameters.notes: Maintain a flat back, keep the front leg straight, and avoid bouncing movements. Focus on feeling a gentle stretch in your hamstrings, not pain.

name: Barbell Squat
overview: The barbell squat is a compound exercise that primarily targets the quadriceps, glutes, and core muscles. It's considered one of the most fundamental movements for building lower body strength and muscle mass. The exercise requires proper form to protect your lower back and maximize muscle activation throughout the movement.

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-3 (3 seconds eccentric, 1 second pause, 3 seconds concentric)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with bodyweight, progress to 50-80% of 1RM for hypertrophy
trainingParameters.duration: 4-6 sets of 8-12 reps for muscle growth
trainingParameters.notes: Maintain proper knee alignment, keep chest up, and avoid letting knees cave inward. Use a rack for safety with heavier weights. Drive through your heels and keep your weight mid-foot.

name: Dumbbell Press
overview: The dumbbell press is a fundamental chest exercise that targets the pectorals, triceps, and anterior deltoids. It's performed lying on a flat bench with dumbbells in each hand, pressing them upward from chest level to full extension. This movement provides excellent chest development while allowing for a greater range of motion compared to barbell bench press.
benefits: Develops chest, shoulders, and triceps strength
Improves overall upper body muscle mass
Supports bone density in upper body
Allows for independent arm movement and coordination

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds down, no pause, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with 40-60% of 1RM, progress to 75-85% for strength
trainingParameters.notes: Keep feet flat on floor, maintain a natural arch in lower back, and control the dumbbells throughout the movement. Use a spotter for heavy attempts and focus on the mind-muscle connection.

name: Deadlift
overview: The deadlift is a fundamental compound exercise that builds total body strength, with emphasis on the posterior chain including hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. It's performed by lifting a loaded barbell from the ground to hip level. Proper form is critical to prevent injury and maximize power output throughout the entire posterior chain.
benefits: Increases bone density throughout the body
Engages core for stability during heavy lifting

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-1 (2 seconds pull, 1 second hold at top, 1 second controlled descent)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight to master form, progress to 70-90% of 1RM
trainingParameters.duration: 3-5 sets of 3-6 reps for strength focus
trainingParameters.notes: Maintain a neutral spine throughout, keep the bar close to your body, and drive through your heels. Don't round your back and avoid jerky movements. Focus on powerful hip extension and keep your chest up.

name: Push-ups
overview: Push-ups are a classic bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, triceps, and core muscles. They involve lowering your body until your chest nearly touches the floor, then pushing back up to the starting position. Push-ups are excellent for building relative upper body strength and developing pressing power.
benefits: Develops pectorals, triceps, and anterior deltoids
Requires no equipment beyond a floor
Excellent for building functional upper body strength
Strengthens core for stability during movement

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds down, no pause, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight initially, add weighted vest for progression
trainingParameters.notes: Keep core engaged, back straight, and lower until your chest nearly touches the floor. Avoid sagging hips and maintain full range of motion. Use assisted variations if needed to build initial strength and perfect form.

name: Pull-ups
overview: Pull-ups are a bodyweight exercise that targets the lats, biceps, and upper back muscles. They involve pulling your body up to a bar using primarily upper body strength. Pull-ups are excellent for building relative strength, developing a V-taper physique, and strengthening the entire upper back.
benefits: Requires minimal equipment beyond a bar
Excellent for building a V-taper physique
Strengthens core for stability during pulling movements

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds pull up, 1 second hold, 2 seconds lower)
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight initially, add weighted vest for advanced progression
trainingParameters.notes: Keep core tight throughout, avoid swinging or kipping, and achieve full range of motion. Use assisted variations (band, machine, or partner assist) if needed to build initial strength before attempting full bodyweight pull-ups.

name: Plank
overview: The plank is an isometric core exercise that strengthens the abdominal muscles, lower back, and stabilizers. It involves holding a push-up position while maintaining tension in the core muscles. Planks are excellent for developing core stability, improving posture, and reducing lower back pain.
benefits: Reduces risk of lower back pain
Can be varied with multiple positions for progression

trainingParameters.tempo: Hold position steadily, breathe naturally
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight only, can add weighted vest for advanced trainees
trainingParameters.notes: Maintain a straight line from head to heels, engage glutes, and don't let hips sag or rise. Focus on deep breathing and progressively increase hold time by 5-10 seconds per week as strength improves.

name: Barbell Bench Press
overview: The barbell bench press is a compound exercise for building upper body strength, primarily targeting the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It's performed lying on a bench while pressing a barbell upward from chest level to full arm extension. The movement requires proper shoulder stabilization and controlled execution for optimal chest and tricep development.
benefits: Develops chest, shoulders, and triceps strength
Improves overall upper body muscle mass
Supports bone density in upper body
Can be varied for different training goals (strength, hypertrophy, power)

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds down, no pause, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with 40-60% of 1RM, progress to 75-85% for strength
trainingParameters.duration: 3-5 sets of 5-8 reps for strength, 8-12 reps for hypertrophy
trainingParameters.notes: Keep feet flat on floor, maintain a natural arch in lower back, and control the barbell throughout the entire movement. Use a spotter for heavy attempts and focus on a controlled eccentric phase for maximum muscle tension.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
overview: The incline dumbbell press targets the upper chest and anterior deltoids. It's performed on a bench set at a 30-45 degree angle, pressing dumbbells from chest level to full extension. This movement emphasizes the upper chest fibers and provides excellent chest development while allowing for a greater range of motion compared to flat bench press.
benefits: Develops upper chest and anterior deltoids
Increases chest muscle thickness and fullness
Allows for greater range of motion than flat bench
Improves upper body pushing strength at different angles
Can help with muscle imbalances by working upper chest specifically
Excellent for chest aesthetics and definition

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds down, no pause, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Set bench to 30-45 degree angle, keep your shoulder blades retracted against the bench, and focus on squeezing your upper chest at the top of the movement. Control the descent and avoid bouncing the weights.

name: Cable Crossover
overview: The cable crossover is an isolation exercise that targets the chest muscles, particularly the inner chest. It's performed by bringing cables from a high position together in front of your body in a hugging motion. This movement provides excellent chest definition and helps develop the pectorals fully.
benefits: Isolates and develops the chest muscles
Targets inner chest for better definition
Provides constant tension throughout the movement
Allows for various hand positions to target different angles
Excellent for chest aesthetics and bodybuilding
Reduces shoulder stress compared to heavy pressing movements

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds bring together, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Step slightly forward into the movement, keep a slight bend in your elbows, and focus on squeezing your chest at the center of the movement. Use a controlled tempo and feel the chest contraction throughout.

name: Dumbbell Fly
overview: The dumbbell fly is an isolation exercise that targets the chest muscles, particularly the outer chest. It's performed lying on a bench with dumbbells, opening your arms wide with a slight bend in your elbows. This movement provides excellent chest stretch and contraction for maximum muscle development.
benefits: Improves chest muscle definition and separation
Allows for great range of motion
Excellent for chest aesthetics and bodybuilding
Reduces shoulder involvement compared to pressing movements

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds down, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light to moderate weight, focus on form over heavy lifting
trainingParameters.notes: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement, focus on feeling the stretch in your chest at the bottom and the contraction at the top. Don't lock your elbows and avoid using momentum.

name: Pec Deck Machine
overview: The pec deck machine is an isolation exercise that targets the chest muscles from a horizontal position. It's performed sitting on a machine with your arms against pads, bringing them together in front of your chest. This movement provides excellent chest contraction and is ideal for beginners learning proper chest training mechanics.
benefits: Isolates and develops the chest muscles
Provides stable and controlled movement pattern
Excellent for beginners learning chest training
Allows for focus on chest contraction
Reduces risk of injury with fixed path of motion
Supports consistent tension throughout the movement

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds bring together, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight to master form, increase gradually
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your back flat against the pad, press with your palms facing each other, and focus on squeezing your chest at the center. Use a controlled tempo and avoid using momentum or jerking movements.

name: Barbell Row
overview: The barbell row is a compound pulling exercise that targets the upper back, lats, and biceps. It's performed by pulling a barbell from the floor toward your lower chest while bent over. Proper form is crucial to protect your lower back and effectively target the upper back muscles for maximum development.
benefits: Develops latissimus dorsi strength and width
Enhances posture by strengthening back muscles
Balances pushing exercises like bench press

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-3 (2 seconds pull, 1 second squeeze, 3 seconds lower)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Maintain a flat back, keep your chest parallel to the ground, and pull your elbows toward your body at the top. Avoid using momentum and focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together. Control the descent to maximize muscle tension.

name: Lat Pulldown
overview: The lat pulldown is an isolation exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi and biceps. It's performed sitting at a cable machine, pulling a bar down toward your upper chest. This movement provides excellent lat development and helps create a V-taper physique while minimizing lower back stress.
benefits: Isolates and develops the latissimus dorsi
Provides constant tension throughout the movement
Reduces lower back stress compared to bent rows

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds pull down, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your chest up and pull the bar down to your upper chest, focusing on driving your elbows down and back. Squeeze your lats at the bottom of the movement and extend your arms fully at the top. Avoid using body English or swinging.

name: Seated Cable Row
overview: The seated cable row is a compound pulling exercise that targets the rhomboids, lats, and traps. It's performed sitting at a cable machine with feet on a platform, pulling a handle toward your lower chest. This movement provides excellent upper back development and helps improve posture.
benefits: Develops rhomboids and upper back muscles
Supports better posture and spinal alignment
Provides stable and controlled movement pattern
Excellent for back thickness and development

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds pull, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your chest up, pull the handle toward your lower chest with a slight lean back, and squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement. Maintain a neutral spine and control the weight throughout.

name: Chin-up
overview: The chin-up is a compound pulling exercise that targets the lats, biceps, and upper back. It's performed by pulling your body up to a bar with your palms facing you and chin above the bar. This movement provides excellent upper back and bicep development while helping improve overall pulling strength.
benefits: Targets lower lats for V-taper development
Strengthens core for stability during pulling movements

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds pull up, 1 second hold, 2 seconds lower)
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight initially, add weighted vest for progression
trainingParameters.notes: Keep core tight throughout the movement, avoid swinging or kipping, and focus on controlled execution. Drive with your elbows and squeeze your back at the top. Use assisted variations if needed to build initial strength.

name: Romanian Deadlift
overview: The Romanian deadlift is a compound exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. It's performed by holding a barbell at hip height with a shoulder-width grip, hinging at the hips, and lowering the bar along your legs. This movement is excellent for posterior chain development and hip mobility.
benefits: Builds tremendous hamstring and glute strength
Improves hip hinge mechanics and mobility

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-3 (3 seconds lower, 1 second squeeze, 3 seconds stand)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight to master form, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout the movement, keep the bar close to your body, and focus on pushing your glutes back. Don't round your back and feel a stretch in your hamstrings. Keep your chest up and shoulders back.

name: Overhead Press
overview: The overhead press is a compound exercise that targets the shoulders, triceps, and core. It involves pressing a barbell or dumbbells from shoulder height to fully overhead. This movement requires excellent shoulder stability and controlled execution throughout the range of motion for optimal shoulder and tricep development.
benefits: Develops triceps and upper chest strength
Can be performed seated or standing for variety

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds up, no pause, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light dumbbells or empty bar, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Keep core tight, avoid excessive lower back arch, and lower the weight under control. Don't lock your elbows at the top of the movement and maintain tension in the working muscles throughout the entire range of motion.

name: Lateral Raise
overview: The lateral raise is an isolation exercise that targets the lateral deltoids. It's performed standing or sitting with dumbbells at your sides, raising your arms out to shoulder height. This movement provides excellent shoulder width and definition, helping create a broader shoulder appearance.
benefits: Isolates and develops the lateral deltoids
Can be performed with various arm positions

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds up, no pause, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light to moderate weight, focus on form over heavy lifting
trainingParameters.notes: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement, maintain a neutral spine, and focus on the lateral deltoid contraction. Don't swing the weights and keep the movement controlled. Raise to shoulder height but don't hyperextend your shoulders.

name: Arnold Press
overview: The Arnold press is a variation of the dumbbell press that targets the chest, front deltoids, and triceps. It's performed starting with palms facing you and rotating them to face you as you press the weights up. This movement provides excellent chest and front shoulder development.
benefits: Develops chest and front deltoids simultaneously
Increases chest muscle fullness and definition
Provides greater range of motion than standard presses
Excellent for chest aesthetics and anterior shoulder development

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds up with rotation, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Start with palms facing you, rotate your wrists to face you as you press up, and rotate back to face you as you lower the weights. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and focus on squeezing your chest at the top. Control the movement throughout.

name: Face Pull
overview: The face pull is an isolation exercise that targets the rear deltoids, rhomboids, and upper back. It's performed pulling a cable or rope attachment toward your face, spreading it apart. This movement provides excellent rear shoulder development and helps improve posture.
benefits: Isolates and develops the rear deltoids
Provides constant tension for shoulder development

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds pull, 1 second spread, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Set the cable at face height with a rope attachment, pull the rope toward your face spreading it apart at the top, and squeeze your rear delts. Keep your core tight and avoid using momentum. Control the return to the starting position.

name: Upright Row
overview: The upright row is a compound exercise that targets the lateral deltoids, traps, and biceps. It's performed standing with a narrow overhand grip on a barbell, pulling it up to chest height. This movement provides excellent shoulder and upper back development.
benefits: Improves upper back thickness and definition

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds up, no pause, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Keep the bar close to your body throughout the movement, pull with your elbows leading the movement, and focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top. Don't swing the weight and keep your torso upright.

name: Barbell Bicep Curl
overview: The barbell bicep curl is a compound isolation exercise that targets the biceps. It's performed standing with a shoulder-width underhand grip on a barbell, curling it up toward your chest. This movement is fundamental for building arm strength and bicep size.
benefits: Builds significant bicep strength and size

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds curl up, no pause, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your elbows tucked to your sides, avoid swinging your body, and focus on the bicep contraction. Control the weight throughout the movement, especially during the lowering phase. Don't hyperextend your lower back and maintain a neutral spine.

name: Hammer Curl
overview: The hammer curl is a bicep exercise that targets the biceps brachialis. It's performed with dumbbells, palms facing each other, curling the weights up. This movement helps develop the outer bicep and provides a thicker arm appearance.
benefits: Targets the biceps brachialis for arm thickness
Increases overall bicep strength and size
Provides greater arm definition and aesthetics

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds curl up, no pause, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light to moderate weight, focus on form over heavy lifting
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your palms facing each other throughout the movement, curl both dumbbells simultaneously, and focus on squeezing your biceps at the top. Control the descent and avoid using momentum. Keep your elbows stationary and focus on the brachialis contraction.

name: Tricep Dip
overview: The tricep dip is a compound bodyweight exercise that targets the triceps, chest, and shoulders. It's performed by lowering and raising your body between parallel bars or on a dip station. This movement is excellent for building upper body pushing strength and tricep development.
benefits: Builds strong triceps and chest muscles
Can be performed with bodyweight or added resistance
Excellent for arm and chest definition

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds down, no pause, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with bodyweight, add weight belt for advanced progression
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your elbows tucked at 45 degrees to your body, avoid locking your elbows at the top, and lower to 90 degrees in your arms. Don't shrug your shoulders at the bottom and maintain tension in your triceps throughout the movement. Keep your torso upright and focus on controlled execution.

name: Skull Crusher
overview: The skull crusher is an isolation exercise that targets the triceps. It's performed lying on a bench with a barbell or EZ-bar, lowering the weight toward your forehead by bending your elbows. This movement provides excellent tricep development and helps build arm mass.
benefits: Targets all three tricep heads effectively
Reduces elbow stress compared to close-grip exercises

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-3 (3 seconds lower, 1 second squeeze, 3 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your upper arms stationary and your elbows tucked to your sides. Lower the weight toward your forehead with control, squeeze your triceps at the bottom, and extend your arms to return to the starting position. Don't flare your elbows and maintain tension throughout the movement.

name: Tricep Pushdown
overview: The tricep pushdown is an isolation exercise that targets the triceps. It's performed standing at a cable machine with a straight or V-bar attachment, pushing the bar down until your arms are fully extended. This movement provides excellent tricep development and helps define the arms.
benefits: Provides constant tension throughout the movement
Reduces elbow stress compared to overhead extensions
Excellent for arm aesthetics and bodybuilding

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds push down, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your elbows tucked to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement. Push the bar down focusing on driving your elbows toward the ground, squeeze your triceps at the bottom, and fully extend your arms. Avoid using body English or swinging and maintain tension in the triceps.

name: Concentration Curl
overview: The concentration curl is an isolation bicep exercise that targets the biceps. It's performed sitting on a bench with your elbow braced against your inner thigh, curling a dumbbell up toward your shoulder. This movement helps develop bicep peak and improves arm aesthetics.
benefits: Enhances mind-muscle connection in the biceps
Excellent for bicep focus and concentration

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds curl up, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light to moderate weight, focus on form over heavy lifting
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your elbow braced firmly against your inner thigh, focus on the bicep contraction, and curl the weight with control. Don't swing your body or use momentum. Squeeze your bicep at the top and lower the weight slowly to maximize muscle tension.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
overview: The overhead tricep extension is an isolation exercise that targets the triceps. It's performed sitting or standing with a dumbbell held overhead, lowering the weight behind your head by bending your elbows. This movement provides excellent tricep development and helps build arm mass.
benefits: Targets the long head of the triceps effectively
Reduces shoulder stress compared to pressing movements
Excellent for tricep focus and development

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds lower, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light to moderate weight, focus on form over heavy lifting
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your upper arms close to your ears and your elbows stationary. Lower the weight behind your head with control, focusing on the tricep contraction. Don't hyperextend your lower back and keep the movement smooth and controlled.

name: Leg Press
overview: The leg press is a compound exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. It's performed sitting in a leg press machine with feet shoulder-width apart, pressing the platform back up. This movement provides excellent lower body strength development.
benefits: Strengthens hamstrings for complete leg development
Improves leg press strength and power
Supports bone density in lower body
Provides stable and controlled movement pattern

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds down, no pause, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your feet flat on the platform and shoulder-width apart. Release the safety bars and lower the platform, pressing back up without locking your knees. Keep your back flat against the pad and focus on the quadriceps contraction. Don't hyperextend your knees at the top.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
overview: The Bulgarian split squat is a unilateral lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps and glutes. It's performed by placing one foot behind you on a bench and lowering your back knee toward the ground. This movement helps develop each leg independently and improves balance.

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-2 (3 seconds down, 1 second pause, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with bodyweight or light dumbbells, progress gradually
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your front foot flat on the bench and your back knee over your ankle. Drive through your front foot to stand back up, keeping your torso upright. Don't let your back knee touch the ground. Focus on controlled movement and engage your glutes throughout.

name: Lunges
overview: Lunges are a unilateral lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. They involve stepping forward into a deep lunge position and returning to standing. This movement improves balance, coordination, and develops each leg independently.
benefits: Can be performed with various forward angles

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-2 (3 seconds down, 1 second hold, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with bodyweight, progress to holding dumbbells or barbell
trainingParameters.notes: Step forward into a controlled lunge, keeping your front knee behind your toes and maintaining an upright posture. Don't let your back knee touch the ground and keep your torso stable. Alternate legs and focus on balanced development.

name: Leg Curl
overview: The leg curl is an isolation exercise that targets the hamstrings. It's performed sitting in a leg curl machine with the pad against your lower legs, curling the weight toward your glutes. This movement provides excellent hamstring development and helps build leg definition.
benefits: Strengthens knee stability and joint health
Complements quad exercises for balanced leg development
Provides constant tension for muscle growth

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds curl up, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Sit comfortably in the machine with the pad against your lower legs. Curl the weight toward your glutes with control, squeezing your hamstrings at the top. Lower the weight with control, avoiding any swinging or bouncing. Don't hyperextend your knees and keep your back flat against the seat.

name: Leg Extension
overview: The leg extension is an isolation exercise that targets the quadriceps. It's performed sitting in a machine with the pad against your shins, extending your legs to straighten them. This movement provides excellent quad development and helps build leg strength.
benefits: Strengthens knee stability and joint health
Improves athletic performance and jumping ability
Reduces risk of knee injuries with proper form
Complements hamstring exercises for balanced leg development

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds extend, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Sit comfortably in the machine with the pad against your shins. Extend your legs with control, squeezing your quads at the top. Lower the weight with control, avoiding any bouncing or jerking. Don't lock your knees at full extension and keep the movement smooth.

name: Calf Raise
overview: The calf raise is an isolation exercise that targets the calf muscles. It's performed standing on a raised surface with heels hanging off, pushing up onto your toes. This movement provides excellent calf development and helps build lower leg strength.
benefits: Isolates and develops the calf muscles
Increases lower leg strength and power
Enhances athletic performance and jumping ability
Complements leg training for complete development

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-1 (2 seconds up, 1 second hold, 1 second lower)
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight only, can add weighted vest for progression
trainingParameters.notes: Stand on a raised surface with your heels hanging off the edge. Push up onto your toes as high as possible while keeping your legs straight. Hold for a moment at the top, focusing on the calf contraction. Lower your heels below the surface level with control. Don't bounce and maintain tension throughout.

name: Hip Thrust
overview: The hip thrust is a compound exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core. It's performed sitting on the ground with your upper back against a bench, rolling a barbell over your hips. This movement provides excellent glute and hamstring development.
benefits: Builds tremendous glute and hamstring strength
Increases lower body power and explosiveness

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds up, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Keep your back flat against the bench and your shoulders stabilized. Roll the barbell over your hips with control. Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line, squeezing your glutes at the top. Lower with control and don't hyperextend your lower back.

name: Front Squat
overview: The front squat is a compound exercise that targets the quadriceps and glutes with emphasis on the quads. It's performed with the barbell resting on your front shoulders in a front rack position. This movement provides excellent quad development and helps build leg strength.
benefits: Builds significant quadriceps strength and size
Increases lower body power and explosiveness
Supports athletic performance and jumping ability
Reduces lower back stress compared to back squats

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-3 (3 seconds down, 1 second pause, 3 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Rest the barbell on your front shoulders in a front rack position with your elbows high and chest up. Keep your torso upright and your weight mid-foot. Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Drive back up keeping your torso upright and your elbows high.

name: Russian Twist
overview: The Russian twist is a core exercise that targets the obliques and abs. It's performed sitting on the floor with knees bent and leaning back slightly, holding a weight in front of your chest. You rotate your torso to one side, then the other, engaging your core throughout.
benefits: Reduces risk of lower back injuries

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds rotate, 1 second hold, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light to moderate weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and leaning back slightly. Hold the weight in front of your chest with both hands. Rotate your torso to one side, then the other, keeping your core engaged throughout. Control the movement and avoid using momentum. Keep your feet flat and focus on the oblique contraction.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
overview: The hanging leg raise is a core exercise that targets the abs and hip flexors. It's performed hanging from a pull-up bar with arms extended, raising your legs until they're parallel to the floor. This movement provides excellent core development and improves overall stability.

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds up, 1 second hold, 2 seconds lower)
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight only, can add ankle weights for progression
trainingParameters.notes: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms extended and your body straight. Raise your legs with control until they're parallel to the floor. Avoid swinging your body and focus on the abdominal contraction. Keep your core tight and don't use momentum. Lower your legs with control.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
overview: The ab wheel rollout is an advanced core exercise that targets the abs, obliques, and lower back. It's performed kneeling with an ab wheel, rolling it forward extending your body. This movement provides excellent core development and helps build abdominal strength.

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds roll forward, 1 second hold, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight only, progress gradually
trainingParameters.notes: Kneel with the ab wheel in front of you. Roll forward extending your body as far as you can while keeping your core tight. Don't let your hips sag and maintain tension in your abs throughout. Roll back to the starting position with control. Avoid arching your lower back and focus on controlled movement.

name: Mountain Climbers
overview: Mountain climbers are a core and cardio exercise that targets the abs, hip flexors, and quads. They start in a high plank position, driving one knee toward your chest and alternating legs in a running motion. This movement provides excellent cardiovascular conditioning and core development.
benefits: Excellent for HIIT and metabolic conditioning

trainingParameters.tempo: Explosive movement, minimize rest between reps
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight only
trainingParameters.duration: 3-5 sets of 20-30 reps for time-based challenge
trainingParameters.notes: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart. Drive one knee rapidly toward your chest, then quickly switch legs in a running motion. Keep your hips level throughout and your core engaged. Focus on explosive power and speed. Modify by stepping back to plank position if needed.

name: Kettlebell Swing
overview: The kettlebell swing is a full-body exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core. It's performed standing with feet wider than shoulders, swinging a kettlebell between your legs. This movement provides excellent power development and improves overall conditioning.
benefits: Builds tremendous glute and hamstring power

trainingParameters.tempo: Explosive swing, control at top and bottom
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, progress to heavy swings
trainingParameters.notes: Stand with feet wider than shoulders, kettlebell between your legs. Hinge at your hips and swing the kettlebell between your legs explosively. Control the swing at the top and bottom. Keep your back flat and core engaged. Avoid rounding your back and use your hips to generate power.

name: Box Jump
overview: The box jump is a plyometric exercise that targets the quads, glutes, and calves. It's performed standing in front of a sturdy box, swinging your arms and jumping onto the box. This movement provides excellent lower body power and explosiveness development.
benefits: Increases lower body explosiveness and power

trainingParameters.tempo: Explosive jump, soft landing, quick reset
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight only, can hold light dumbbells
trainingParameters.notes: Stand in front of a sturdy box with feet shoulder-width apart. Swing your arms and jump onto the box with both feet. Land softly with both feet fully on the box, keeping your knees slightly bent to absorb impact. Step down and reset quickly. Focus on explosive power and soft landings. Don't lock your knees on landing.

name: Farmer's Walk
overview: The farmer's walk is a full-body strength exercise that targets the traps, forearms, and core. It's performed picking up heavy dumbbells in each hand and walking with a tall posture and tight core. This movement builds tremendous grip strength and overall body stability.
benefits: Builds tremendous grip and forearm strength

trainingParameters.tempo: Controlled walking, maintain upright posture
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to heavy
trainingParameters.notes: Pick up heavy dumbbells in each hand with a tight grip. Keep your shoulders back and down, maintain a tall posture with your core engaged. Walk with controlled steps and avoid swinging your body. Keep your head neutral and look forward. Focus on grip strength and walk with purposeful steps.

name: Step-up
overview: The step-up is a unilateral lower body exercise that targets the quads and glutes. It's performed holding dumbbells and standing in front of a raised platform, stepping up onto it. This movement improves balance, develops leg strength, and enhances athletic performance.

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds up, no pause, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with bodyweight or light dumbbells, progress gradually
trainingParameters.notes: Hold dumbbells and stand in front of a raised platform. Step up onto the platform with one foot, driving through your raised foot to stand up completely. Step down and alternate legs. Keep your torso upright and your core engaged. Focus on controlled movement and balanced development.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
overview: The dumbbell shrug is an isolation exercise that targets the upper traps. It's performed standing with dumbbells at your sides, shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears. This movement helps build trap thickness and improves shoulder aesthetics.
benefits: Isolates and develops the upper traps
Excellent for trap development and thickness

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds shrug up, 1 second hold, 2 seconds lower)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light to moderate weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip. Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears, focusing on the trap contraction. Hold at the top for a moment and lower with control. Avoid rolling your shoulders and keep the movement smooth. Don't use momentum or excessive weight.

name: Good Morning
overview: The good morning is a compound exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. It's performed with a barbell on your upper back as for a squat, hinging at the hips and lowering your torso. This movement provides excellent posterior chain development and hip mobility.
benefits: Reduces risk of lower back injuries

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-3 (3 seconds down, 1 second squeeze, 3 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight to master form, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Rest the barbell on your upper back as for a squat, maintaining a slight bend in your knees. Hinge at your hips, pushing your glutes back, and lower your torso until nearly parallel to the floor. Drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top. Keep your chest up and avoid rounding your lower back.

name: Cable Crunch
overview: The cable crunch is an isolation exercise that targets the abs. It's performed kneeling in front of a cable machine with a rope attachment, pulling the rope down and crunching your torso. This movement provides excellent ab development and helps define the midsection.
benefits: Provides constant tension throughout the movement
Excellent for ab aesthetics and development

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds crunch down, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Kneel in front of a cable machine with a rope attachment. Hold the rope with both hands at your chest. Pull the rope down and crunch your torso toward your knees, squeezing your abs at the bottom. Return to the starting position with control. Avoid using momentum and focus on the abdominal contraction.

name: Sled Push
overview: The sled push is a full-body exercise that targets the quads, glutes, calves, core, chest, triceps, and shoulders. It's performed behind a sled with arms extended, driving your legs into the ground to push the sled forward. This movement builds tremendous lower body power and overall conditioning.

trainingParameters.tempo: Explosive drive, steady push
trainingParameters.weight: Add plates to sled for resistance
trainingParameters.notes: Position yourself behind the sled with arms extended against the handles. Keep your core tight, back flat, and drive through your legs powerfully into the ground. Push the sled forward with strong, controlled strides. Keep your head neutral and focus on explosive leg drive. Maintain tension throughout the push.

name: Battle Ropes
overview: Battle ropes are a cardio and conditioning exercise that targets the shoulders, abs, arms, and core. It's performed holding one rope in each hand, alternating raising and lowering them rapidly to create waves. This movement provides excellent cardiovascular conditioning and upper body endurance.
benefits: Excellent for HIIT and metabolic conditioning

trainingParameters.tempo: Explosive alternating waves, maintain rhythm
trainingParameters.weight: Use bodyweight only
trainingParameters.notes: Hold one rope in each hand with a neutral grip, standing with feet shoulder-width apart. Alternate raising and lowering each arm rapidly to create waves in the ropes. Maintain a slight squat position and keep your core engaged throughout. Focus on explosive power and consistent rhythm. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid excessive tension.

name: Preacher Curl
overview: The preacher curl is an isolation bicep exercise that targets the biceps. It's performed sitting on a preacher bench with your upper arms on the pad, curling a barbell or dumbbells up. This movement helps develop bicep peak and improves arm aesthetics.
benefits: Enhances mind-muscle connection in the biceps
Excellent for bicep focus and peak development

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds curl up, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Sit comfortably on a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad. Grip the barbell or dumbbells with a shoulder-width underhand grip. Curl the weight toward your shoulders, focusing on the bicep contraction. Squeeze at the top and lower with control. Avoid swinging or using body English. Keep your elbows stationary and focus on form.

name: Hack Squat
overview: The hack squat is a compound exercise that targets the quads and glutes with less lower back stress. It's performed on a hack squat machine, lowering your body by bending your knees. This movement provides excellent quad development and helps build leg strength.
benefits: Excellent for quad development and size

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-3 (3 seconds down, 1 second pause, 3 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Position yourself correctly on the hack squat machine with your shoulders under the pads. Lower your body by bending your knees, keeping your back flat against the pad. Push back up to the starting position with control. Don't lock your knees at the top and focus on quad contraction. Maintain controlled movement throughout.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
overview: The dumbbell wrist curl is an isolation exercise that targets the forearms. It's performed sitting on a bench with your forearms on your thighs, holding dumbbells with an underhand grip, wrists hanging off your knees. This movement helps develop forearm strength and improves grip.

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds curl up, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds down)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Sit on a bench with your forearms resting on your thighs. Hold dumbbells with an underhand grip, wrists hanging off your knees. Curl the weights up using only your wrists, keeping your forearms stationary. Focus on forearm contraction and control the movement. Avoid using body English or excessive weight.

name: Incline Bench Press
overview: The incline bench press is a compound exercise that targets the upper chest, anterior deltoids, and triceps. It's performed on a bench set at a 30-45 degree angle, pressing a barbell upward. This movement emphasizes the upper chest and helps create a fuller chest appearance.
benefits: Develops upper chest and anterior deltoids
Allows for greater range of motion than flat bench

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds down, no pause, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width. Unrack the bar and lower it to your upper chest. Press the bar back up to full extension. Keep your feet flat and shoulder blades retracted. Control the descent and focus on squeezing your upper chest.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
overview: The dumbbell pullover is an exercise that targets the chest and lats. It's performed lying across a bench, holding a dumbbell over your chest, and lowering it behind your head. This movement provides excellent chest stretch and helps develop the upper body.

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds down, 1 second stretch, 2 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Use light to moderate weight, focus on form and muscle contraction
trainingParameters.notes: Lie across a bench holding a dumbbell over your chest. Lower the dumbbell behind your head with a slight bend in your elbows. Feel the stretch in your chest and lats. Pull the weight back over your chest with control. Keep your core engaged and avoid using momentum. Focus on controlled movement and muscle stretch.

name: Landmine Press
overview: The landmine press is a unilateral pressing exercise that targets the anterior deltoids and triceps. It's performed holding one end of a barbell anchored to the ground, pressing it up and away from your shoulder. This movement provides excellent shoulder development and helps build upper body strength.

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-0-2 (2 seconds up, 1 second press, 2 seconds lower)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with moderate weight, progress to 60-80% of 1RM
trainingParameters.notes: Hold the end of the barbell at shoulder height. Press the barbell up and away from your shoulder. Fully extend your arm at the top. Lower with control and repeat. Keep your core tight and avoid excessive leaning or rotating. Focus on controlled movement and shoulder contraction.

name: Single-Leg Deadlift
overview: The single-leg deadlift is a compound exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and core. It's performed standing on one leg, holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand, hinging forward and extending your free leg. This movement provides excellent unilateral leg strength and improves balance.

trainingParameters.tempo: 3-1-3 (3 seconds down, 1 second squeeze, 3 seconds up)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, progress to moderate
trainingParameters.notes: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand. Hinge forward, extending your free leg behind you. Lower the dumbbell toward the ground with control. Drive your hips forward to return to standing. Keep your core engaged and avoid rotating your torso. Focus on balanced development and controlled movement.

name: Pallof Press
overview: The pallof press is a core exercise that targets the obliques and abs. It's performed standing perpendicular to a cable machine at chest height, holding a handle at your chest with both hands. It involves pressing the handle straight out in front of you and resisting rotation. This movement provides excellent oblique development.

trainingParameters.tempo: 2-1-2 (2 seconds press, 1 second squeeze, 2 seconds return)
trainingParameters.weight: Start with light weight, focus on form
trainingParameters.notes: Stand perpendicular to a cable machine at chest height. Hold the handle at your chest with both hands. Press the handle straight out in front of you, focusing on the oblique contraction. Resist rotation and return to your chest. Keep your core engaged and avoid excessive weight. Focus on controlled movement and oblique isolation.
